title: Vinod Kumar Dabas vs V D Institute Of Technology & Ors. on 6 May, 2022
full_text: Vinod Kumar Dabas vs V D Institute Of Technology & Ors. on 6 May, 2022 IN THE COURT OF MS DIVYA ARORA, MM (NI ACT)-01, SOUTH-WEST DISTRICT: NEW DELHI CC No.30491-18 Under Section 138 of N.I. Act In the matter of: VINOD KUMAR DABAS S/o Shri D S Dabas R/o E-38, Budh Vihar Phase I, Delhi -86. ... Complainant Versus 1. V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY Krishan Vihar, Near Sultanpuri, Bus Terminal Delhi - 110 086. 2. SHRI JAI KISHAN (DIRECTOR) V. D. Institute of Technology Krishan Vihar, Near Sultanpuri Bus Terminal Delhi -110 086. Also at :- Shri Jai Kishan S/o Late Shri Rattan Lal R/o A-140, Raj Park Sultanpuri, Delhi. ... Accused persons Date of Institution : 14.09.2018 Date of Judgment : 06.05.2022 JUDGMENT 1. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that the accused no.2 and complainant were having family relations and accused no.2 was also Ex VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.1 of12 MLA of the area. It is further alleged that accused no.2 approached the complainant for a friendly loan of Rs.7,38,000/- as he was facing financial difficulties. It is further alleged that keeping in view the friendly relationship and assurance of the accused, the complainant disbursed a friendly loan to the accused and he issued three PDC in favour of the complainant. One of the cheque issued in the month of April 2018 for Rs.1,50,000/-, 2 nd Cheque bearing no.000253 dated 12.05.2018 for Rs.2,40,000/- and 3rd Cheque bearing no.000256 dated 10.08.2018 of Rs.3,48,000/-, all drawn on Bank of Baroda, Sultanpur Majra, Delhi and the said loan was given to accused without interest. Accused no.2 assured the complainant that the said Cheques will be honoured on their presentation. However, on presentation of Cheque for Rs.1,50,000/-, the same got dishonoured and this fact was told to the accused by complainant and thereafter the accused repaid the said sum in cash to the accused and the complainant returned the said Cheque to the accused. It is further alleged that on presentation of Cheque bearing no.000253 of Rs.2,40,000/-, the same was returned dishonoured vide return memo dated 01.06.2018 with the remarks ''STOP PAYMENT'' and therafter on 10.08.2018, complainant presented the Cheque in question i.e. bearing no.000256 dated 10.08.2018 of Rs.3,48,000/- and same was also returned dishonoured with the remarks ''Stop Payment'' vide return memo dated 13.08.2018. Upon this, the complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 23.08.2018 and an amended legal demand notice dated 28.08.2018 to the accused and on failure of accused to pay the cheque amount within the mandatory period of 15 days, the complainant has moved this court with a complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.2 of12 (hereinafter referred as " NI Act "). Original Cheque is Ex.CW1/1, Return memo is Ex.CW1/2, Legal notice is Ex.CW1/3, Amended Statutory Notice is Ex.CW1/4, Speed post and registered AD are Ex.CW1/5 (colly) and Tracking report is Ex.CW1/6. 2. On finding of prima facie case against the accused, summons were issued and the accused appeared before this court on 04.05.2019. 3. The notice under section 251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (" Cr.P.C .") was framed against the accused vide order dated 03.12.2019 to which he pleaded not guilty. The accused deposed that,''The Cheque in question bears my signatures. However, I have not filled the particulars namely, name of payee, date and sum. I had issued the Cheque in question in blank signed condition to the complainant as security for goods to be supplied by the complainant to me. I owe no legal liability. The complainant has supplied me counterfeit goods. I had received the legal notice sent by the complainant''. 4. The complainant adopted his pre-summoning evidence tendered by way of affidavit(CW1/1) as his post-summoning evidence. 5. After framing of notice, complainant was cross examined by counsel for accused. Thereafter, the complainant evidence was closed and the matter was listed for statement of accused under Section 313 CrPC. VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.3 of12 6. Statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 CrPC read with Section 281 Cr.P.C. on 26.10.2021 wherein all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against the accused was put to him to which he stated that,'' I have not taken any loan from the complainant. I have not issued any Cheques in regard to the loan amount. However, I have issued three Cheques in lieu of purchase of AC, Fridge, fans. I do not remember whether I have given Rs.1,50,000/- in cash to the complainant. It is correct that I had received the legal notice sent by complainant. However, I am not abble to recall exactly which legal notice I had received. I had even given reply to the said legal notice denying my liability. I am managing V D Insitute of Technology. I know the complainant for the last five or six years. I needed some electrial appliances for my school i.e. R D International School, Rohini. Complainant said that he will provide the said appliances. I issued three post dated cheques in the month of March 2018 (volt.I do not remember the exact month). After that, complainant did not deliver any electric appliances. Therefore, I asked bank to stop the payment. I have not taken any loan from the complainant. I further submit that the complainant is intentionally acusing me in the present case''. 7. Accused in his defence, examined himself as DW1, DW2 and DW3 and they all were cross examined by Ld. Counsel for complainant. Thereafter DE was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments. VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.4 of12 8. Thereafter, the Ld. Counsel for complainant and the accused were heard at length in the present case and the matter was reserved for Judgement. 9. Before proceeding to the merits of the case, it is important to lay down the basic provision of law with respect to Section 138 NI Act which is as follows:- Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 makes dishonour of cheques an offence. It provides that ''where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall without prejudice to any other provisions of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both''. 10. In order to ascertain whether the accused has committed on offence u/s 138 NI Act, the following ingredients constituting the offence have to be proved:- (a) The drawer of the cheque should have issued the cheque for the discharge, in whole or in part of a legally enforceable debt or other liability. VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.5 of12 (b) The cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank. (c) The drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money within fifteen days of the receipt of the notice from the payee or the holder in due course demanding the payment of the said amount of money. It is only when all the above mentioned ingredients are satisfied that the person who has drawn the cheque can be set to have committed an offence u/s 138 NI Act. 11. It is important to recall Section 118 of the Indian Evidence Act 1872 and Section 139 of the N.I Act here. Section 118 (a) of the Act provides that until the contrary is proved, it shall be presumed that ''that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred, was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration''. Further, Section 139 of the Act lays down that ''it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is provided, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability. 12. In the case of Hiten P. Dayal Vs Bratindranath Bannerjee (2001) G SCC 16, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India had observed that ''Because both sections 138 and 139 CrPC required that the court shall VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.6 of12 presume the liability of the drawer of the cheque for the amount for which the cheques are drawn as noted in State of Madras Vs A. Vaidhyanatha Iyer AIR 1958 SC 61, it is obligatory on the court that raise this presumption in every case where the factual basis for raising of the presumption has been established. It introduces an exception to the general rule as to the burden of proof in criminal cases and shifts the onus on to the accused''. 13. Further, in the case of K. N. Beena Vs Muniyappan AIR 2001 SC 2000, it was established as follows ''In complaint under Section 138 the court has to presume that the cheque had been issued for a debt or liability, this presumption is rebuttal, however, the burden of proving that the cheque has not been issued for the discharge of debt or liability lies on the accused''. 14. Let us begin by examining the first issue i.e. service of legal notice. Accused in his notice framed u/s 251 CrPC and at the stage of evidence has admitted to the receiving of legal notice. As the receipt of notice is admitted, an important ingredient constituting the offence u/s 138 NI is proved. 15. The core issue that arises for consideration whether the cheque in question was issued by the accused in discharge of his liability. 16. The accused has admitted his signatures on the cheques in question at every stage; from notice u/s 251 , Cr.P.C. to his examination u/s 313 , Cr.P.C. and finally in his evidence, giving rise to the presumption in VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.7 of12 favour of the holder of the cheque under S. 139 of NI Act. Thus, unless the contrary is proved, it shall be presumed that the complainant received the cheques in discharge of the debt/ liability from the accused. The standard of proof for rebuttal is on preponderance of probabilities. As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in decision cited as K.N. Beena vs Muniyappan And Another ; (2001) 8 SCC 458, in order to rebut the presumption, mere denial by the accused will not suffice. The accused must prove by leading cogent evidence that there was no debt/ liability. 17. Major argument led by accused's counsel is that the legal demand notice in the present case does not comply with the legal requirement of proviso (b) to Section 138 NI Act as in the legal demand notice, the cheque amount was not demanded rather a vague amount of Rs.5,88,000/- was demanded. The relevant extract from the amended legal demand notice which is Ex.CW1/4, is as under :-"I hereby call upon you through this legal notice to pay to my client a sum of Rs.5,88,000/- alongwith damages, interest......." 18. Condition precedent in both the proviso (b) and (c) of Section 138 envisages "Payment of the said amount of money". The said amount of money undoubtedly would be the amount of the cheque. As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Central Bank of India and Anr. vs. Saxons Farms and Ors. , AIR 1999 SC 3607, wherein it was stated that :The object of the notice is to give a chance to the drawer of the cheque to rectify his omission. The demand in the notice has to be in relation to 'said amount of money' as described in the provision. The expression 'payment of any amount VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.8 of12 of money' as appearing in the main portion of Section 138 of the Act goes to show it needs to be established that the cheque was drawn for the purpose of discharging in whole or in part of any debt or any liability, even though the notice as contemplated may involve demands for compensation, costs, interest etc. The drawer of the cheque stands absolved from his liability under Section 138 of the Act if he makes the payment of the amount covered by the cheque of which he was the drawer within 15 days from the date of receipt of notice or before the complaint is filed. 19. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Suman Sethi vs. Ajay K. Churiwal and another , AIR 2000 SC 828 held that :The legislative intent as evident from Section 138 of the Act is that if for the dishonoured cheque the demand is not met within 15 days of the receipt of the notice the drawer is liable for conviction. If the cheque amount is paid within the above period or before the complaint is filed, the legal liability under Section 138 ceases to be operative and for the recovery of other demands such as compensation, costs, interests etc. separate proceedings would lie. The accused/drawer of the cheque is absolved from the criminal liability if he makes the payment of the cheque amount i.e. said amount within stipulated period of 15 days from the date of receipt of notice. If in the legal demand notice, more amount is demanded or the cheque amount is not demanded, that would not advance the legislative intent. The purpose of giving him (accused herein) notice prior to filing of complaint case under section 138 of NI Act is to give him an opportunity to make the payment of the cheque amount. If the amount demanded in the legal demand notice is vague amount, it would virtually amount that no such VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.9 of12 opportunity is being granted to him. 20. Hon'ble Apex Court in K.R. Indira vs. Dr. G. Adinarayana , AIR 2003 SC 4689 again reiterated the following :The notice in question is imperfect in this case not because it had any further or additional claims as well but it did not specifically contain any demand for the payment of the cheque amount, the non-compliance with such a demand only being the incriminating circumstance which expose the drawer for being proceeded against under Section 138 of the Act. 21. In the present case also, legal demand notice and amended notice is imperfect as it did not specifically contain any demand for the payment of the cheque amount. The cheque amount is "Rs.3,48,000/-" and the amount demanded in the legal demand notice and amended legal demand notice is "Rs.5,88,000/-". Non payment of cheque amount i.e. Rs.3,48,000/- within the stipulated period would only bring the accused within the clutches of Section 138 of NI Act. But as in the instant case, some different amount i.e 5,88,000/- is being demanded, condition of proviso (b) is not complied with. 22 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in M/s Rahul Builders vs. M/s Arihant Fertilizers & Chemical & Anr, decided on 02.11.2007 wherein it was held that :Unless a notice is served in conformity with Proviso (b) appended to Section 138 of the Act, the complaint petition would not be maintainable. The Parliament while enacting the said provision consciously imposed certain conditions. One of the conditions was service of a notice VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.10 of12 making demand of the payment of the amount of cheque as is evident from the use of the phraseology "payment of the said amount of money". Such a notice has to be issued within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of information from the bank in regard to the return of the cheque as unpaid. The statute envisages application of the penal provisions. A penal provision should be construed strictly; the condition precedent wherefor is service of notice. It is one thing to say that the demand may not only represent the unpaid amount under cheque but also other incidental expenses like costs and interests, but the same would not mean that the notice would be vague and capable of two interpretations. An omnibus notice without specifying as to what was the amount due under the dishonoured cheque would not subserve the requirement of law. 23. As the legal demand notice in the instant case is not in conformity with the proviso (b) of Section 138 of NI Act and the cheque amount is not demanded, condition precedent given in proviso (b) not fulfilled, therefore, main provision u/s 138 would not apply. Both proviso (b) and (c) are interrelated as if the legal demand notice is not valid and sum demanded in legal demand notice is not the cheque amount, failure to make payment of the said amount of money as envisaged in proviso (c) cannot be imputed on the accused because the accused will only be in a position to make payment when the said amount of money (cheque amount) is demanded from him. 24. In view of the above discussion, this court has come to the conclusion that Section 138 NI Act would not apply in this case. Accused no.1 VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.11 of12 and 2 are acquitted for the offence u/s 138 NI Act. 25. File be consigned to record room. Decided on 06.05.2022 Announced in open court. (DIVYA ARORA) MM (NI Act)-01/SW/DWK New Delhi VINOD KUMAR DABAS VS V D INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & ORS. CC NO.30491-18 Page no.12 of12
